industry.why: Underweight, carried, on the special topic of 30-Oct-26 on the Defence de-rating; the conversion question is still open: Jefferies (Ismail, 26-Nov) is 'nervous' ahead of Rheinmetall's capital markets day on 27-Nov, expects the 2030 revenue guide cut to 35 to 40 billion euros and says the sector cannot recover without Rheinmetall, while Kepler (26-Nov) is constructive on Indra and Goldman (Jaisson, 20-Nov) favours Aerospace and Defence among Cyclicals; the capital markets day's outcome and the Bundestag vote did not reach the pack. Relative strength F (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; F prior), both sectors D or F. Defence rose 6.8% over the five sessions to 27-Nov leading a rebound of November's losers, which is the counter-case on the row, not a reading. No live holding (Theon has left the book), no Pool name. Back to C if relative strength leaves F with the 2030 guide reset read; to F on a signed Ukraine settlement followed by defence fund outflows.

sector.why: Underweight, carried: the land and ammunition names here face Rheinmetall's expected 2030 revenue guide cut to 35 to 40 billion euros (Jefferies, Ismail, 26-Nov), with the capital markets day's outcome not in the pack; relative strength D (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; D prior). Counter-case: large, proven, government-contracted cases are what a risk-off market is meant to pay for, and Jaisson (Goldman, 20-Nov) favours Aerospace and Defence. Back to C when relative strength leaves D or F with the 2030 guide reset read.

geography.why: Double Underweight, carried, now on fresh evidence rather than the stale spread: France's forward-looking PMI fell to 46.2 to 46.8, near its record low, 'a deepening downturn' (S&P Global via Pivotus, 23-Nov; Goldman Economics, 24-Nov), Pivotus calls it 'a disaster', Macron is considering a constitutional 'golden rule' if markets stay unstable in January with Le Pen leading the polls (Pivotus, 23-Nov), and Stehn (Goldman, 22-Nov) expects France to stagnate until its elections. The premium in basis points was unread for a fourth week, so last week's staleness rule (to D if unread again) is overtaken by the political and activity evidence, said plainly. 15 Pool stocks are French-listed, most of them global businesses. Counter-case: a top letter on a country whose listed companies earn mostly abroad, and the mid-2027 election is far away. To D when the premium is read under 120 basis points for a month with the PMI off its low; to C under 100.
